second_reasoning: I checked that #192092 added a duplicate `closeSessionTitle` property and #192046 added the `copied === false` comparison. The fix restores TypeScript and lint checks while preserving the displayed copy and pairing behavior.

The October 27 diff added `display: grid;` to the existing `.chat-activity-group` without defining a column track, letting Safari and Firefox size the implicit track to the unwrapped summary. The before-side CSS already capped both the group and its summary without that intermediate grid track, and September tests confirm the collapsed summary already existed. The fix PR measured the overflow on the later layout, but it did not test the October commit’s parent in a browser.

The fix shows that Telegram clears the typing indicator on delivery while OpenClaw keeps its four-second gate, suppressing the first cue on an immediate follow-up. The September account-throttler diff moved an existing gate from bot-core, and the October refactor retained the same interval. The older diffs were unavailable, so I could not verify when the defect first appeared or whether immediate follow-up typing had previously worked.

I checked the original settings diff and confirmed that the permissions view returned the inspection error and Retry before checking whether inspection data was missing. The tab-unification commit removed `if (props.inspectionError) { return renderRetryError(props.inspectionError, props.onRetryInspection); }` from `renderAccess`, leaving the missing-data branch to show a skeleton after a failed request. The grouped settings and Solid rewrites preserved that behavior.

Standalone plugin pruning already used the selector, and the preceding implementation fed native resolution with static imports or a scope-aware loader scan. The later commit added `onLiteralCall: (specifier) => literalCalls.add(specifier)` and `new Set([...staticImports, ...literalCalls])`, sending ordinary arguments such as `.` and `.sqlite` into the existing native resolver and explaining the reported Bun storage exhaustion. I verified the earlier filtering in the diffs, but a pre-change Bun run on the same build output was unavailable, and the fix also addresses a separate stale filename lookup.

The September diffs already show the route selecting Playwright when a connection is cached and Playwright calling `page.screenshot` without first activating the tab. The focus-preservation commit kept activation for raw CDP captures in headless Chrome. Earlier diffs needed to establish when the Playwright failure began were unavailable, so I could not verify whether the affected path ever worked.

The fix’s tests show that the 20,000-character limit could cut off a network page while leaving its continuation cursor visible. The earliest readable renderer diff already contains the truncating branch, and the September optimization retained it. The older runtime diffs were unavailable, so I could not verify when that behavior first reached paginated results or whether those results had previously worked.

The pre-fix manager stored the Activity with `lifecycleOwner = owner` and left that reference in place after idle destruction. I checked the blame diffs and the manager and runtime history, but the available diffs did not establish when the stale reference first became possible, and relevant older diffs were unavailable.

The commit introduced slow chat-send phase accounting and added `phase?.mark("preparation")` in `onSessionPrepared`, with `diagnostics.finish()` at agent startup or dispatch settlement. When steering skipped the startup callback, the preparation scope could stay open through the full reply. I checked that the later steering diagnostics change relabeled the stage while retaining the settlement cutoff, but could not fully confirm that the original steering path could await a full prepared reply.

The original Files disclosure diff passed `() => ({ open: props.open, active: props.active, instant: props.instant })` to the measurement helper and checked `next === applied`, so equal reactive invalidations produced a fresh object, bypassed the guard, and briefly cleared then restored `hidden`. I checked that the original Review disclosure shipped with the same pattern and that the later consolidation carried it forward. The fix also removes redundant shell `inert` writes from separate changes.

The September diffs already show explicit compiles generating a fresh publication ID and writing a new cache entry, and the October teardown diff shows the existing deletion of the predecessor. I found no earlier working reuse path, and the pre-September diffs for the original persisted cache and dashboard publication were unavailable, so I could not verify whether replacement shipped with the feature.

The failed Code Mode test queues corrections inside the request hook introduced by this commit. Its diff adds `const requestMessages = await beforeRequest(signal);` after the steering checkpoint and proceeds to model dispatch without checking steering again, so corrections accepted during that hook missed the upcoming request from the day it shipped. I also checked the earlier `prepareContinuation` diff, which created a similar gap on a separate path.

I checked that the Systems phone viewer already offered Actual in an 88 px native selector with `padding: 0 6px`, which left room for the full label. The later commit changed the selector to `class="settings-select desktop-sizing"`, applying the shared `padding-right: calc(26px + 0.5em)` and one-line clamp while keeping the 88 px width, leaving the 42 px text area where the fix reproduced `Act…`.

The introducing diff replaced recursive deletion with paced batches and added `const hasIoPressure = createHostIoPressureProbe();` as the gate for continuing. I checked the earlier worker and the probe implementation: the earlier worker had no pressure gate, and the new gate could let unlinking continue while btrfs metadata reservations were high because it checked I/O stalls and commit latency without reading the reservation counter.

The original restart-resume implementation followed registered requester links in a `for (;;)` loop, which let it reach the ordinary root through a visible spawned child. I checked that visible dashboard children predated that implementation and that the causing diff replaced the loop with `while (isSubagentSessionKey(root.sessionKey))`. That guard stops at a visible child's dashboard key, so the true root never gets a restart marker.

The original macOS supervisor retried child exits with bounded backoff, and I verified that the intervening refactor preserved that behavior. The causing diff added `if case .terminated(.signaled(SIGILL)) = failure` with an early `return` before the retry counter, so a single SIGILL stopped recovery. This explains the macOS retry regression that the fix reverses alongside adding persistent crash reporting.

The commit introduced the compact device-path form with `{t("newSession.deviceFolderPath")}` as bare label text above an input whose text was inset by 8 px, so the label was misaligned from the form’s first version. I verified the introducing JSX and CSS and checked the separate mobile search selector changes, whose origin remains unverified.

The September 12 diff shows that the prior global regex already rescanned the remaining text at each unmatched `@[`, so escaped-label support did not introduce the quadratic behavior. The October refactor moved the same parser into the activity builder, and the original mention-support diff was unavailable, so I could not verify which commit first introduced the defect.

The October 24 diff adds `options.askUserAvailable && !hasNativeQuestionOptIn(...) ? { "tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled": false }`, which explains why the native tool was disabled while catalogue guidance still appeared. The same commit documents that native questions already failed under the normal Default-mode restriction, and the September 11 diff shows that Default guidance already mentioned the tool, so the checked history does not establish when the mismatch began or that it previously worked.

The commit moved `const registry = prepareOpenClawAgentDatabaseRegistrySnapshotRead(...)` ahead of the existing storage-preparation wait and added `registry.assertCurrent()` before `capturedSources` was updated with the qualified file identities, so a valid cold registration could invalidate the read. I checked that the prior path waited for pending preparation before establishing the registry witness, and a later focused bisect independently identified #197510 as the first failing first-chat authorization boundary.

The original Advisor controller used `: "fork_failed"` as its catch-all and logged that outcome as a review failure, so expected Codex policy refusals were misreported from launch. I verified that the fork dispatcher already routed reviews through `/btw` with its existing policy guards and that the October 16 rewrite preserved the same classification.

The fix replaces `resourcesPromise ??= createCuaExecutionResources()`, which cached the first rejection and made retry and close rethrow it after the filesystem was repaired. File history points to the August 15 commit that introduced first-use initialization, and the two later refactor diffs leave that cache untouched. The August diff is unavailable, so the attribution rests on the commit subject and file history.

The commit that introduced worker-backed external plugin preparation added `const root = createPluginSourceCaptureRoot(storage.stateDir, "plugin-preparation-");` on the Gateway thread before dispatching work. I checked that the fix removes that host-side allocation and that the PR’s injected `mkdtempSync` delay stalled the Gateway on the parent. The native-root path acquired the same exposure separately when #177067 moved native allocation into a host callback.

The fix and its persistence test show that Agents API omitted prior transcript messages and tool outcomes when creating a native session or returning to a retained one. The September onboarding guide describes same-runtime continuation, and the October diffs I checked showed no earlier working cross-runtime handoff. The original harness diff was unavailable locally, so I could not verify whether the omission shipped with the harness or arose later.

The Solid migration carried forward the Lit root’s cold-start splash and reconnect routing, and the fix changes tests that explicitly expected the splash or sign-in during a retry. I checked the earlier draft-retention change and the commit that added the HTTP startup wait, but neither establishes when an already-open chat first lost its shell or draft during a Gateway restart.

The #199123 diff removed `-webkit-user-select: none` from `.chat-thread` and added `.chat-thread` to the `-webkit-user-select: text` rule, letting WebKit select a newline when the user double-clicks the gap. I checked the prior text-only CSS and its tests for unpainted turn gaps and blank double-clicks, though the exact WebKit gesture was only documented against main after #199123.

The original Systems sidebar hid the session list and rendered its own machine inventory. The October 11 diff replaced `renderSidebarScope(this)` with `renderSessionListToolbar(...)` immediately above the container hidden by `contextualSidebar`, exposing the Sessions owner picker, filter, and new-session control on Systems. The avatar symptom came from a separate later change, `b4bf350c7b0d`, whose new click handler treated every open `sessions` view as eligible for the agent menu.

The parent diff shows that the existing CLI maintenance-lock contention path previously returned a retry message without reading the lease. This commit added `captureStalledGatewayStartup(env)?.description` to that path, and its new helper called `readGatewayOwnerLease({ env, current: true })` for owners past five minutes. I checked the SQLite reader diff and confirmed that without `allowNativeRead`, this lookup takes the full snapshot path.

The reported 4.9-second delivery delay prompted new instrumentation that measures worker event-loop activity and logs it for slow deliveries. The product diff leaves dispatch and execution behavior unchanged, and the sole blame candidate added thread IDs for diagnostics without showing a change that could explain the delay.

The fix reproduces a write that reports success even though the Markdown reader cannot read the key back. The October 15 diff shows that the writer already passed the key directly into `frontmatter: [...ast.frontmatter, { key, value, line: 0 }]` and serialized it via `rebuildMdRaw`. The original feature and early parser diffs were unavailable, so I could not verify whether the mismatch shipped with the feature or arose later.

The commit introduced managed Serve identity in operator hellos, but its resolver returned `undefined` when `!origin?.startsWith("https://")`, and `sendGatewayHello` registered a renewal listener only inside `if (identity)`. I checked the introducing publication diff and confirmed that publishing Serve only called `previous?.abort()`, leaving hellos sent while no route was published without a signal to trigger reconnection.

The pre-change status code already read the plugin ledger for drift, and I checked that the reader used the native read-only path when called without the option. The commit added `artifactPreservingReadOnly: true` to that existing call, selecting the snapshot path and allowing an interrupted copy to leave a partial database behind.

The package diff changes `"@trycua/cua-driver": "0.36.0"` to `"@trycua/cua-driver": "0.37.0"`, whose Markdown default leaves the existing adapter without the structured `elements` it uses to mint references. Earlier tests and docs show that element references predated the upgrade, and the fix reports that explicitly requesting `tree_format: "elements"` restored them on Linux. The available evidence does not include a native Linux run on 0.36.0.

The release qualification failures occurred when transient ClawHub outages outlasted the existing 1s/3s/10s retry schedule and the endpoints recovered shortly afterward. The intervening diffs preserved that schedule, and the fix adds a 30-second retry with a test that succeeds after four HTTP 500 responses.

September documentation and tests already show Undo waiting for a completed archive and then sending a second Gateway request to restore the session. The August commit b4104e29b5ff70e88abf719fd430e60b0841db96 says it added stopping and draining active work before archiving, but the older diff was unavailable, so I could not verify whether Undo previously preserved running work.

The synchronous replay code selected and checked the user anchor in one call, while the October reader refactor shows an already-asynchronous selection followed by strict transcript-version validation. The September async refactor is a plausible source of the race, but its diff was unavailable, so I could not verify the breaking line. The October retry patch covered final consumption only, leaving the initial failure in place.

The sanitizer already used `failedSteps.slice(-3)` to retain recent failures, so it dropped the initiating failure once three later failures followed it. The October 2 diff adds `result.steps.push({ name: "gateway migration recovery", … exitCode: 1 })` on the recovery path after a refused database rollback, adding one of the three later failures that displaced the trigger in the reported case.

The original rehearsal snapshot copied SQLite databases and only transformed the shared database. I checked that the later cold-storage commit introduced rows with `storage: "file"` and `archive_blob: null`, so the existing snapshot began carrying references without their payloads. The bundle shows that Doctor could hit those missing files through either of two repair paths, and the report leaves the exact path unconfirmed.

The earlier Activity controller and its replacement both scheduled reads on session changes and cleared the displayed error when a read started. The trigger commit added `throw sessionMutationForbiddenError(...)` for guests opening another person's timeline, so the existing refresh logic began replacing that settled denial with loading placeholders on unrelated session events.

The original capture kept all declared roots in `roots: [...roots].toSorted()` and filtered SQLite sidecars out of `entries`, which worked for sidecars found inside directory roots. The trigger added Memory Core’s `collectBackupResources` loop, which declared the database and its suffixed paths as separate file roots, exposing the mismatch when manifest validation required an entry for each root.

The earlier reply-deduplication diff and replay tests show that matching a saved reply against the current stream removed the live bubble. The later commit changed that comparison to `self.liveText(self.displayedStreamingAssistantText)`, so pacing could hold back the last words and leave both bubbles visible when the saved reply arrived. The same diff added `.defaultScrollAnchor(..., for: .sizeChanges)` and made ordinary text growth skip timeline updates, which the simulator report ties to replies streaming below the composer.

The earlier design commit explicitly added `margin-block-end: 2px` to give the reply more breathing room and updated the browser test to expect a 10px gap instead of 8px. The fix removes the following bubble’s top margin at the collapsed-summary boundary and changes the expected gap to 4px, establishing a new spacing preference.

The causing diff wrapped the existing `maybeRestartService` call in `await forward(() => ...)` and added `for (const stop of admission.forward) { stop(); }` to the signal handler. I checked the removed lines and confirmed that verification previously ran outside this cancellable scope and the old signal handler exited after settlement, so it could not strand readiness polling with every native service check cancelled. The patch also fixes a separate admission timeout whose introducing diff was unavailable.

The extension manifest diff upgrades `@openai/codex` from `0.164.0` to `0.169.0`, while the earlier observer and its tests were designed for structured spawn errors and exit code 1. The fix PR reproduced the new launcher emitting a fatal `process.execve` header and terminating with `SIGABRT` on Node 24, a dependency behavior the existing exit-code check could not handle.

The commit that introduced 24-hour scratch cleanup scanned checkout `.openclaw/tmp` and skipped host temp entries unless they matched `^node-coverage-.+`, leaving ordinary agent validation temp trees outside cleanup from day one. I checked the cleanup diff, the later prompt change that advised keeping inherited temp paths, and the fix's core exec test, which the PR reports failed on the base until exec was wired to checkout scratch.

The September 7 diff added the web `/settings` fallback as `redirect({ ...location, pathname: pathForRoute("chat", context.basePath) })`, and the September 16 diff separately moved relocated-section redirects from the Settings component into route loaders. The fix’s tests reproduce the outgoing-page remount on the pinned baseline, but the route and outlet history I checked does not establish whether those redirects caused remounts when introduced or whether a later rendering change made them do so.

The commit that introduced live chat automation cards set `retryable: true` in the catch block for every non-aborted `cron.get` error, including the not-found response for a deleted job. I checked that the original card showed Retry whenever `state().retryable && !state().loading` and that c9cc12844c7d preserved that condition.

The provider-runtime commit introduced sidecar coverage reporting for `memory forget` with `emitMemoryCoreSidecarNotice(slotOwner, { json: Boolean(opts.json) })`, and its documentation confirms the notice went to stderr in JSON mode. The fix diff and CLI capture show that stdout serialized only `report`, so a saved JSON report omitted the selected provider and deletion scope from the start.

The fix confirms that iOS offered OpenClaw for selections the extension could not send, including four photos or a video. The file history identifies the original Share extension and a later change that blocked sends when attachments were omitted, but the blobs for both diffs are unavailable, so I could not verify whether either selection had ever worked or which commit introduced the mismatch.

The fix and its integration test show that a direct call to a tool available through Code Mode fell through to the generic “Tool not found” error because the session installed a deferred resolver only when directory tools were directly callable. I checked the Code Mode and session setup history, but the original Code Mode diff was unavailable and the readable diffs did not establish when this rejection behavior first appeared.

I checked the introducing diff, which added interrupted-updater recovery and gated the durable stop check on `if (updaterStopped)`, leaving helper-stopped services exposed to a restart after a later operator stop. The same diff initialized `terminalRuntimePath` to the staged runtime and switched to the installed writer only after recovery returned, so a schema-changing repair that threw left terminal settlement using the old writer. It also introduced `restoreRepairGateway` with an ownership branch that threw a plain `Error`, causing an unverified service to fail an otherwise completed repair.

This commit introduced focus before finger release with `pointerOrigin.focus({ preventScroll: true })` in `pointerdown`, allowing the keyboard to move the composer before Chrome dispatched the compatibility `mousedown`. I checked that the inherited guard only canceled `click`, after `mousedown` could steal focus, and that the introducing test did not simulate a keyboard viewport change between touch start and release.

I checked the commit diff and verified that the existing keyboard-dismissal step used an app-relative tap before the commit replaced it with `app.scrollViews["chat-transcript"].coordinate(withNormalizedOffset: CGVector(dx: 0.99, dy: 0.05)).tap()`. The fix PR measured 22.625 seconds across three transcript lookups during tap synthesis, a cost the old app-relative tap avoided by construction. The bundle contains no timing run from before the candidate commit.

The October blame candidate replaced an existing `access was revoked` branch with a lookup that returned the same message. The September 13 diff shows that allowed navigation already retired page reads while preserving tab authority, but the August diffs needed to establish when that rejection first produced the misleading message were unavailable.

The parent-side diff shows that changed command checkpoints already synchronized guest files into the canonical workspace without a filesystem snapshot. The causing commit added `await nativeWorktreeFilesystem.copy(projectionPath, root, options)` to the new btrfs checkpoint path and removed the capture afterward, introducing the filesystem-wide transaction and cleanup work behind the reported Gateway stalls. Later commits narrowed snapshot use to large or slow checkpoints and changed when cleanup ran.

The introducing diff registered `kind: "session:report"` and mounted it with `return staticHtml` inside the existing saved-height plugin cell, where oversized content scrolled internally. I checked the original report styles and the later phone table change, whose `block.columns.length > 3` condition excludes the fix’s failing three-column table. The pre-September mobile grid diff was unavailable, so the launch behavior is inferred from the surviving diffs.

The product and test diffs introduce an optional invitation input that commits membership with mention involvement and publishes the resulting membership changes. The PR’s main-base comparison shows that existing membership and access flows passed, and the human-mention caller was planned for a later PR.

That commit introduced socket-bound dashboard startup credentials with `LegacyCredentials.waitForInvalidation`. The fix shows that full auth equality governed WebView replacement, so retiring those credentials before the successor socket authenticated could discard the queued input. The earliest readable follow-up already shows socket-owned projections in the reconnect path, but missing blobs prevented checking the original WebView replacement diff directly.

Before #193548, archive reads called `sweepMaterializedArchiveCache(cacheDir)`, which deleted cache entries older than 24 hours with `fs.rmSync(entry.path, { force: true })`. The #193548 diff removed that call and the sweep when it switched to direct streaming, leaving existing plaintext caches without automatic cleanup until Doctor added it.

The fix moves the same survivor scan ahead of SQLite BEGIN, shortening the measured writer hold while preserving deletion and retained-history behavior. I checked the November 3 diff and its predecessor: the CTE replaced an existing in-transaction survivor scan, and the benchmark compares the fix with its immediate baseline, leaving any historical slowdown unverified.
